description: On-demand harness to run bun test inside the cam-worker container, re-baseline v0.60.0 failures, and guard/fix them to green.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed the bun test summary format the harness must parse: standalone ' N pass' / ' N fail' / ' N skip' lines plus a 'Ran N tests across M files. [time]' footer; the process exits non-zero only when there are failures (skips/todo never fail the run). AI-agent quiet output (CLAUDECODE=1 / AGENT=1) hides passing/skipped detail but keeps summary stats and full failure detail intact, so failing test names are always printed and parseable.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [scripts/file-size-budget.json:96]: `bun run check:all` FAILS (exit 1) at the file-size gate: US-002's staged edits grew three test files past their budget ceilings without bumping the budget file. Actual (line-count + 1): test/dashboard.test.ts 1452 (budget 1440), test/integration/review-verdict-handback.test.ts 136 (budget 134), test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts 69 (budget 61). This violates US-001 AC9 and US-002 AC10 ('Full quality spine green'), and the [oracle: bun run check:all] named-command oracle failed at Layer B. Fix: set the three ceilings to 1452 / 136 / 69.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [scripts/test-in-container.ts:130]: parseBunOutput fails to extract failing test names from real `bun test` output. Real bun prints `(fail) <name>` (and `(fail) <name> [Nms]` under CLAUDECODE=1) in the non-TTY docker-exec capture path, but the regex matches `\s+✗\s+<name>(\s+\(Nms\))?`, a marker bun never emits there. Verified: running the branch parser on real captured output returns failingTests:[]. The unit-test fixtures in test/test-in-container.test.ts use the fictional ✗ format, so the name-extraction tests (US-001 AC1/AC2) are false-greens and the feature is non-functional in production (operator sees fail count but not which tests failed). Fix: match `^\((fail|todo)\)\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[\d+.*ms\])?\s*$` and record a real bun fixture.

userStories.title: Build the on-demand in-container test harness
userStories.description: As a container-mode maintainer, I need a repeatable on-demand script that runs bun test inside the cam-worker container and fails only on real test failures, so container mode has a trustworthy regression check that never becomes a Docker-requiring CI gate.
acceptanceCriteria: A new script `scripts/test-in-container.ts` ensure-ups the cam-worker container (reusing the existing ensure-container path) and then runs `bun test` inside it via `docker exec` against `/workspace`, capturing pass/fail/skip counts and the names of any failing tests. [oracle: file-assert grep -q '/workspace' scripts/test-in-container.ts && grep -q 'bun' scripts/test-in-container.ts && grep -q 'test' scripts/test-in-container.ts]

The harness parses the Bun summary lines (' N pass' / ' N fail' / ' N skip') and extracts failing test names from the printed failure blocks; the parse logic is unit-tested against a recorded Bun-output fixture using injected fakes, with no real Docker daemon touched. [oracle: bun test]

The harness exit code is non-zero if and only if there are in-container test FAILURES; a run with only skips (fail count 0) exits 0. Both branches are asserted by unit tests injecting fake bun-test output. [oracle: bun test]

The harness is NOT registered as a CI gate: it is absent from the GATES manifest in `scripts/check-all.ts` and from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (macos CI has no Docker daemon, the CAM-178 trap). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'test-in-container' scripts/check-all.ts .github/workflows/ci.yml returns no match]

The container ADR `docs/adr/0003-worker-isolation-boundary-dev-container.md` gains a pointer instructing the operator to run `bun scripts/test-in-container.ts` before shipping any container-mode change, and states that this regression protection is on-demand (not a CI gate). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'test-in-container' docs/adr/0003-worker-isolation-boundary-dev-container.md]

The committed `worker_isolation` default remains host: `scripts/cam/project.toml` does not set `worker_isolation = "container"` (the harness brings the container up itself). [oracle: file-assert grep for 'worker_isolation.*container' in scripts/cam/project.toml returns no match]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine green (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Core deliverable, fully deterministic (no live Docker needed to complete this story; the live run happens in US-002). Files: new `scripts/test-in-container.ts`, new `test/test-in-container.test.ts` (mirror test/check-all.test.ts at test/ root, NOT test/scripts/), edit `docs/adr/0003-worker-isolation-boundary-dev-container.md`. Reuse the existing container plumbing: `ensureWorkerContainer` / `makeProductionEnsureContainerFn` (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts), `DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME='cam-worker'` and `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG='cam-worker:latest'` (src/supervisor/worker-container.ts). Build the docker-exec argv NON-interactively (plain `docker exec cam-worker bun test`, NO `-it`) so stdout is capturable; do NOT reuse dockerExecWrap (src/supervisor/docker-exec.ts), which is `-it` for the TUI worker. The container WORKDIR is already `/workspace` (Dockerfile line 72), so bun test runs against the bind-mounted repo by default. Follow the DI pattern of scripts/check-all.ts / ensure-container.ts: injectable spawnFn/ensureFn/exec seams so unit tests assert argv + parse + exit-code with fakes and never touch a real daemon (patterns.md: injectable onResults / SpawnFn conventions; scripts/**/*.ts are knip entry points). Parser gotcha (from the Bun docs consulted): parse the standalone summary lines and the failure blocks; when CLAUDECODE=1/AGENT=1 is set in the container env, bun test hides passing/skip detail but keeps summary + failure detail, so failing test names remain parseable. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard every regex capture group. Optional convenience: add a `test:container` script to package.json, but do NOT add it to the GATES manifest or ci.yml (CAM-178). Do not add em-dash to the ADR (project rule).

userStories.title: Re-baseline v0.60.0 in-container failures and drive them to green
userStories.description: As a container-mode maintainer, I need the real in-container failure list reproduced on the v0.60.0 image, each failure classified and either guarded or fixed, and the host-vs-container count discrepancy accounted for, so `bun scripts/test-in-container.ts` reports 0 failures with only documented skips remaining.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the harness on the v0.60.0 image records the authoritative in-container baseline in a new deep-dive `docs/container-test-baseline.md`: pass/fail/skip counts plus every in-container FAILURE enumerated as file plus test name (this replaces the stale '2957 pass / 10 fail vs 3012 green' number). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'pass' docs/container-test-baseline.md and the doc contains a per-failure list or an explicit '0 failures' statement]

Every captured in-container failure is labelled env-specific vs real-toolchain-gap in the baseline doc, each with a one-line evidence-based reason. [oracle: file-assert grep -Eq 'env-specific|toolchain' docs/container-test-baseline.md; reviewer-judgment for the reasoning quality]

Each env-specific failure is converted to a documented skip using the existing per-file `test.skipIf(!probe)` convention with a module-level availability probe (e.g. `Bun.which(tool) !== null` or `spawnSync(tool,['--version']).status === 0`), never a blanket disable; the skip reason is auditable in the test file. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'skipIf' on each touched test file]

Each real gap whose fix is one story or less is fixed in this PR (e.g. add the missing binary to `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, or fix an unguarded shell-out or uid/ownership/path assumption); any gap whose fix exceeds one story is filed as a new referenced CAM issue via /cam-issue and cited in the baseline doc, never left silently failing. [oracle: reviewer-judgment; file-assert on any .devcontainer/Dockerfile change and on the CAM-NNN reference in docs/container-test-baseline.md]

The difference between the host total and the in-container (run plus skip) total is fully accounted for: every non-run test maps to a documented intended skip (e.g. the ~30 tmux-absent skipIf tests) in the baseline doc, with no silent disappearance. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'tmux' docs/container-test-baseline.md and a reconciliation table is present; reviewer-judgment]

After the fixes, the harness run on v0.60.0 reports 0 failures (`bun scripts/test-in-container.ts` exits 0); remaining non-run tests are documented skips. tmux is NOT added to the worker image solely to satisfy tmux integration tests (green counts documented skips, operator decision i). [oracle: bun scripts/test-in-container.ts (exit 0); file-assert grep for a tmux apt package in .devcontainer/Dockerfile returns no match]

CONTINGENCY: if the v0.60.0 baseline shows 0 in-container failures, criteria 2 to 4 are satisfied vacuously; the baseline doc records the '0 failures' result plus the count reconciliation, and criterion 6 still holds (harness exits 0). [oracle: reviewer-judgment; file-assert docs/container-test-baseline.md exists]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine green (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: This is the single Docker-dependent story; it runs the US-001 harness against the live daemon on the operator's host (default host isolation means the worker runs on the operator's macOS where Docker Desktop is available; container mode was validated live this session per CAM-185/journal). Files: new `docs/container-test-baseline.md`, whatever `test/**` files need skipIf guards, and possibly `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` (a missing binary is the cheapest real-gap fix). GOTCHAS: (1) STALE NUMBERS: '2957/10 vs 3012' is from the CAM-175 pre-jq/pre-CAM-185 ceremony; host is now 3070 and the real in-container failure list is unknown and likely smaller, possibly 0 (contingency). (2) The ~45 uncounted tests are mostly tmux-absent skips (30 skipIf(!tmuxAvailable)) plus possible jq skips; those are SKIPS not failures. Do NOT add tmux to the worker image (the worker never uses tmux at runtime). (3) Docker-driving tests inject a fake probe/spawn (no real daemon), so they pass in-container: do NOT assume they are failures. (4) The genuine failures are what the skip/fake convention failed to catch: an unguarded shell-out or fs/uid assumption, a probe testing the wrong thing, or a real uid/ownership/path difference under the re-homed bun user in /workspace. (5) node_modules on the bind-mounted /workspace are the host's (macOS-arm64) but the container is linux: if bun test in-container fails on native/platform resolution, that is itself a real gap the harness surfaces; classify and fix or file it, do not pre-solve here. Skip convention is per-file `test.skipIf(!flag)` with a module-level probe (see test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts jqAvailable = Bun.which('jq') !== null; test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts tmuxAvailable = spawnSync('tmux',['-V']).status===0); there is no shared helper, follow it. Regression protection stays on-demand (macos CI has no Docker daemon, CAM-178). Do NOT commit a worker_isolation flip. No em-dash in the persisted baseline doc (project rule); route the cycle narrative to journal.md at cycle close, not into the baseline doc.

parseBunOutput fails to extract failing test names from real `bun test` output. Real bun prints `(fail) <name>` (and `(fail) <name> [Nms]` under CLAUDECODE=1) in the non-TTY docker-exec capture path, but the regex matches `\s+✗\s+<name>(\s+\(Nms\))?`, a marker bun never emits there. Verified: running the branch parser on real captured output returns failingTests:[]. The unit-test fixtures in test/test-in-container.test.ts use the fictional ✗ format, so the name-extraction tests (US-001 AC1/AC2) are false-greens and the feature is non-functional in production (operator sees fail count but not which tests failed). makeDefaultExecFn calls spawnSync without an explicit maxBuffer; the Node default is 1MB. For a regression harness whose whole point is to detect failures, output truncation would fail-open (summary lines at the end get cut, parseBunOutput returns all zeros -> exit 0). Non-TTY output is compact today so this is unlikely, but set maxBuffer (e.g. 64MB) to harden against silent fail-open.

The heading 'US-001 skips: new tmux-absent guards (6)' is inaccurate: review-verdict-handback.test.ts and sendkeys-submit.test.ts already had test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable) on main; US-002 only fixed the module-level probe robustness (Bun.spawnSync ENOENT throw). They are not newly-added guards.
